title: Understanding N-gram Limitations
text: Consider how N-grams treat sequences of letters. What happens when you have segments that are not exactly $$3$$ letters long?

title: Non-Consecutive Segments
text: Think about how N-grams might mistakenly group non-consecutive letters together. How could this affect the interpretation of DNA sequences?

title: Overlapping Segments
text: N-grams can create overlapping segments. How might this be problematic when analyzing DNA sequences?

title: Wrap-Around Segments
text: Consider how N-grams might incorrectly interpret the end of a sequence as wrapping around to the beginning. Why is this an issue for DNA sequences?

title: Identifying N-gram Issues
text:
Identify which of the following are true about the limitations of using N-grams for DNA sequences:
$$1$$. Segments of non-consecutive letters would be included.
$$2$$. Segments with $$1$$ or $$2$$ letters have no meaning.
$$3$$. Overlapping segments would be included.
$$4$$. DNA does not "wrap around", but N-gram would capture "wrap-around" segments.
